content: {"id": "2630b6ba-e1fa-4a34-84c2-b6b0379dbe68", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "A RHEL 8 EC2 instance fails patching with 'Read-only file system' writing to /var/lib/rpm. dmesg shows 'EXT4-fs error ... remounting filesystem read-only' and several 'blk_update_request: I/O error' entries on the root device. Should I just remount it read-write and retry?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "6f995de5-b396-44cc-ab90-45eb438b4c35", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "RHEL EC2 instance filesystem corruption EXT4 errors"}]}

{"id": "4af582bb-f5d3-4df0-9ec9-b45d9d1efd22", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "No — remounting read-write and retrying is likely to make things worse here, not fix anything.

**Why not:** EXT4 auto-remounts to read-only as a *protective* response when it detects an I/O error on the block device (those `blk_update_request: I/O error` lines in dmesg are the root cause, not a side effect). The filesystem went read-only to prevent further corruption after a failed write. If you force a read-write remount without addressing the underlying storage/IO problem:

- The same I/O errors will likely recur, potentially mid-write to the RPM database (`/var/lib/rpm`), which can corrupt it further
- You could end up with an unbootable instance or an RPM database that's silently inconsistent even if yum "succeeds"

**What's actually happening at the host level:** this looks like a classic case of a disk/volume-level I/O fault (bad EBS volume state, underlying hardware issue, or a volume that's hit a stall/degraded condition) rather than something `yum`/`dnf` itself can resolve. Remounting treats the symptom, not the cause.

I have a dedicated runbook for exactly this class of problem — host-level preconditions that block patching before the package manager even runs (read-only remounts from I/O errors, inode exhaustion, OOM kills, SELinux denials, etc.). It specifically calls out that a read-only FS from I/O errors must **not** just be remounted blindly.

Want me to pull up that instance and walk through the proper diagnosis (checking EBS volume status/health, confirming no pending hardware retirement, verifying the I/O errors have stopped before any remount) instead of just forcing it read-write?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
